skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

llm.summary: This frog-analysis skill is not proven malicious, but it silently manages identity, stores tokens, and sends media/auth data to under-disclosed HTTP development endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The code detects the OpenClaw workspace, reads environment identity fields, reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, and uses a shared workspace data directory; some workspace awareness is coherent for an OpenClaw skill, but reusing an ambiguously named API-key file as account identity is disproportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer backdoor or remote code retrieval was found, but the analysis requirements declare yaml==6.0.3 instead of the expected PyYAML package, creating install reliability and dependency-confusion risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses cloud history access and automatic local attachment handling, but it instructs agents not to ask for or show identity values and does not clearly disclose silent registration, workspace identity reuse, token persistence, private development endpoints, or allowed network domains.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates or reuses a shared SQLite database under the workspace data directory and stores remote access tokens and open tokens as ordinary string fields, with no evident encryption, retention controls, or user-facing reset/logout flow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote media analysis and cloud history lookup fit the stated purpose, but the bundled shared code adds broad authenticated HTTP helpers, generic video/common-AI analysis behavior, account handling, and report retrieval that are not narrowly scoped to frog skin moisture assessment.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Expect uploaded frog images or videos and history queries to contact a remote service, create or reuse a local identity, and persist account tokens locally. The publisher should remove development HTTP endpoints, require HTTPS and endpoint allowlisting, make account linking explicit, secure or avoid token storage, document retention/deletion, and fix the YAML dependency.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Authenticated API use and history lookup are partly purpose-aligned, but automatic identity creation, token handling, and broad shared network helpers are under-scoped for the advertised frog assessment workflow; treated as a Review concern rather than proof of tool poisoning.
[YR4] unexpected: I did not find artifact-backed offensive-tool or exploit content at the cited SKILL.md location; this match appears unsupported and did not drive the verdict.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The inherited analysis component is generic video/common-AI infrastructure while the wrapper sets the frog scene code; this is not inherently malicious, but it confirms capability drift and weaker scoping than the manifest suggests.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Generic authenticated HTTP/CRUD helpers and identity/token persistence are broader than needed for a narrow animal-image assessment skill and are not adequately constrained by domain or operation.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifacts do not provide a clear least-privilege permission boundary for filesystem, workspace identity, database, and network access.
[SQP-1] expected: Triggering on frog media analysis is expected, but automatic broad history retrieval such as displaying all reports lacks visible user scoping such as date range, enclosure, or identity confirmation.
[SQP-2] expected: Local media handling and cloud history queries are disclosed at a high level and fit the workflow, but storage location, retention, transmitted identity fields, and endpoint details are under-disclosed.
[T09] unexpected: The effective common configuration selects env: dev and overrides service URLs to private HTTP endpoints; the request helper also stores and forwards tokens, including to absolute URLs without host validation.
[T05] unexpected: The code automatically reads workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt and submits the resolved value as openId and mobile during silent registration, which exceeds the identity access users would expect from frog media analysis.
[T08] unexpected: The requirements file uses the ambiguous package name yaml while the common module uses PyYAML, confirming the dependency naming concern without showing malicious install code.
